walkthroughs.body_html:
Resistance is how hard it is for current to flow.

Long thin wires have high resistance. Short thick wires have low resistance.

Bigger resistance = smaller current (for the same voltage).

Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

The UK mains supply is 230 V alternating current (AC) at 50 Hz.

Plugs have three pins: live, neutral, earth.

A fuse melts if too much current flows, breaking the circuit and protecting you.

Always handle electricity with dry hands and respect - 230 V can kill.

Earth has its own giant magnetic field, like a bar magnet inside.

That's why a compass needle (a tiny magnet) lines up pointing north.

Confusingly, Earth's geographic north is a magnetic south pole - because the north of a compass is attracted to it!

The field also shields us from harmful solar particles.

mcqs.q: Why does Faraday's law include a minus sign (Lenz's law)?
options: The minus sign is a mathematical convention with no physical meaning.
It reflects them back the way they came.
The minus sign means the current flows backwards through the wire.
The induced current flows in a direction that opposes the change in flux that produced it — a consequence of energy conservation.
